new_statements.locator: p. 94 (Appendix E, Comparative word lists, 'Symbols'); Lemolang (LEM) word list stress marks at p. 143 item 90, p. 179 items 160-161, p. 199 item 200; Lemolang list metadata Appendix C pp. 89-91 (list 32, Sabbang, Luwu, December 1982, C. Grimes, reliability 'good')
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (216 pp., native text layer; book page = PDF page - 8). Book p. 94 (PDF 102) rendered and read as an image: under APPENDIX E, COMPARATIVE word LISTS, SYMBOLS, the entry for the apostrophe reads exactly "Stress in South Sulawesi languages usually occurs on the penultimate syllable. In such cases it is not marked in the word lists. Where stress deviates from the normal pattern or where stress may be unclear due to double vocoids, etc., it is marked with an apostrophe preceding the stressed syllable." Quote verbatim. The Lemolang-specific marks were checked on page images: p. 143 (PDF 151) LEM row, third column ('here'): 'indene; p. 179 (PDF 187) LEM row, columns 1-2 ('why', 'how'): 'ma…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the penultimate syllable by default; in the ~200-item Lemolang list this holds for all but three forms, which are marked as deviating or unclear: 'indene 'here' (p. 143), 'mapai 'why' and 'how' (p. 179), both with stress on the antepenult/first syllable, and bo'toai 'drop' (p. 199), where the stressed syllable is the third from the end or the mark reflects a vowel sequence.
new_statements.exceptions: Lemolang: 'indene 'here', 'mapai 'why'/'how', bo'toai 'drop' carry a non-default stress mark. The survey also notes (p. 96) that Selayar, another South Sulawesi language, sometimes shows antepenultimate stress; nothing of the kind is stated for Lemolang in the 'unique phonetic features' section (pp. 96-97).
new_statements.domain_note: A survey-wide statement covering the 30+ South Sulawesi word lists in the book, applied to Lemolang through the marking convention in the phonetic word list (citation forms elicited in December 1982; 'slightly phonemicised' phonetic transcription). Word level, isolated elicited forms; no phrase-level information.
new_statements.identity_note: Same variety as lemo1243: the Grimes & Grimes 1987 word list (LEM) was collected at Sabbang, Kabupaten Luwu (the Baebunta area) in December 1982 by C. Grimes (Appendix C, pp. 89-91); van der Veen 1929 calls it 'Lemolangsch' of Waiboenta (villages Sassa', Rompu, Kapuli). No dialect split is reported anywhere. Caveat for the catalog: the stress sentence is a blanket statement over all South Sulawesi word lists in the survey, not a Lemolang-specific paragraph; the Lemolang-specific evidence is the marking convention applied to the ~200-item Lemolang list (only three forms carry a non-default stress mark).

sources.note: p. 94 (Appendix E, Symbols): stress in South Sulawesi languages usually penultimate, unmarked in the word lists; deviations or unclear cases (double vocoids) marked with an apostrophe before the stressed syllable. Lemolang list (LEM): only 'indene 'here' (p. 143, item 90), 'mapai 'why'/'how' (p. 179, items 160-161) and bo'toai 'drop' (p. 199, item 200) are marked; all other Lemolang forms unmarked = penult. pp. 96-97 'unique phonetic features' has no Lemolang entry; pp. 53-54 Lemolang classification entry has no phonology. Verified on page images.
